summary: Intermittent 5xx (502/503) errors observed during short high-concurrency bursts
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (notably LuminaDocs) reported periodic 502/503 responses from the API during short-lived bursts of high concurrency (10s of requests per second sustained for ~30-90s). Errors are not continuous but spike coincident with traffic surges. Impact: request failures for production traffic, degraded app UX for end users.

Observed behavior:
- 502 and 503 responses returned by api-gateway with upstream error messages referencing broken pipe / connection reset in gateway logs.
- Serving-runtime instances show transient process restarts for a subset of pods during the largest bursts.
- No recent customer-side config changes reported.

Scope: Multiple LuminaDocs routes and a few other enterprise customers in us-east during their scheduled traffic bursts. Not observed in staging.

Initial hypothesis: Connection pooling / keepalive exhaustion at api-gateway or transient runtime OOMs causing process restarts and upstream 502s. Another possibility: ephemeral networking flaps between gateway and serving runtime under bursted load, resulting in upstream reset.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Send concurrent generation requests to a redwood-v2-small endpoint at 60 concurrent streams for 60 seconds
2. Observe gateway response codes and serving-runtime pod logs
3. Repeat with progressively lower concurrency to find threshold where 502s cease
logs:
Gateway excerpts (us-east):
[03-11T14:03:22Z] api-gateway: upstream response error: connection reset by peer (code 502)
[03-11T14:03:24Z] gateway: upstream closed connection prematurely while reading response
Serving-runtime excerpts: 
[03-11T14:03:23Z] runtime-worker: process pid=2345 terminated unexpectedly (signal 9)
[03-11T14:03:23Z] runtime: kv-cache cleanup starting; active sessions dropped: 12
Resource metrics (cluster-autoscaler): CPU spike to 85% on affected nodes, short-lived pod restart count +3 during incident window
comments: [2026-03-11 14:12] Customer (LuminaDocs) - Sarah J: We're seeing this during our indexing job bursts. Request IDs: rID-6a9f, rID-7b2e. Affecting ~8% of requests during the 30-90s windows.
[2026-03-11 14:18] Support - Aisha P: Acknowledged, opening incident. Asking for request IDs and timestamps; adding SRE on call.

[2026-03-11 14:25] SRE - Riley C: Correlating logs and metrics. Noted gateway upstream resets timed with runtime process deaths. Collecting full debug logs and heap profiles from affected runtime pods.

[2026-03-11 15:10] SRE - Riley C: Temporary mitigation applied: rate limit soft-cap for LuminaDocs routes at gateway during bursts; increased idle connection pool size between gateway and runtime. Monitoring for reduction in 502s.
[2026-03-11 18:02] Customer - Sarah J: After the temporary soft-cap we saw error rate drop from ~8% to ~1.2% during a subsequent scheduled burst. Thanks for the quick action.
[2026-03-12 09:20] Support - Aisha P: Marking investigation continuing; planning longer-term fix with runtime team.

[2026-03-12 11:40] Runtime Dev - Lucas M: Reproduced locally with stress harness. Found race in connection teardown handling when process is signalled; patch in review: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123
investigation_notes: 1) Correlation between gateway upstream 'connection reset' and runtime worker process exits suggests upstream provider side instability rather than pure gateway bug.

2) Heap and thread dumps from affected runtime processes show burst-related memory spike in tokenization path; not sustained OOM but memory pressure triggers kernel OOM-killer on some hosts under constrained node memory settings.
3) Load-balancer health checks did not show node-level failures; pod restarts were single-process only, pointing to in-process crash rather than node failure.
4) Gateway connection pool defaults were insufficient for the burst concurrency pattern (short lived fan-out), leading to connection churn and higher probability of encountering a closing connection.
5) Autoscaler reacted but with delay; node provisioning lag allowed pressure windows where multiple runtime processes experienced reduced available memory.
6) Repro harness: stress-generator run at 70-80 concurrent streams reproduces 502s within 25-40s on similar instance sizes used by LuminaDocs.
resolution:
Workaround and long-term fixes applied:
- Immediate mitigations (rolled within 1 hour): gateway soft-cap for affected routes, increased idle connection pool and keepalive settings between api-gateway and serving-runtime, temporary bump of pod memory requests for affected node pool. Result: error rate dropped from ~8% to ~1% for subsequent bursts.
- Short-term patch (deployed to canary): updated runtime connection teardown to handle mid-flight resets gracefully (PR #4123).
- Medium-term actions: autoscaler tuning to be more aggressive for sudden fan-out patterns, increase default pod memory on heavy-tokenization models, and add a new alert for rapid spike in upstream connection resets.
- Follow-up: postmortem scheduled; customer will be notified of permanent fix timeline and tested before removing soft-cap.
postmortem_followup_items: Schedule postmortem and RCA (owner: Riley C)
Promote runtime PR #4123 to prod after canary validation (owner: Lucas M)
Adjust default gateway connection pool and keepalive config and document for runbook (owner: Networking team)
Tune autoscaler thresholds for short, high-concurrency spikes (owner: Infra)
Run workload replay with LuminaDocs sample traffic to verify stability (owner: Solutions Eng)
Inform LuminaDocs of timeline for permanent fix and arrange follow-up call (owner: CS)
Create alert: >3 upstream connection resets per minute for a given route (owner: Observability)
Review node sizing for tokenization-heavy models (owner: Runtime/Provisioning)
